messages.subject: Multinomial IRT model
parts:
Greetings. I am trying to run a multinomial 2 dimensional IRT model. 
There are total 66 items (questions) and the range of categories per question is from 2 to 7. So I had to write a quite complicated model.
I am getting an error on the last line where I have categorical(softmax). The error message looks like following.

When I run categorical(softmax))

No matches for: 

  softmax(real)

Available argument signatures for softmax:

  softmax(vector)


When I do categorical_logit

SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

No matches for: 

  int ~ categorical_logit(real)

Available argument signatures for categorical_logit:

  int ~ categorical_logit(vector)
  int[] ~ categorical_logit(vector)

require real scalar return type for probability function.

Here is my code.

data {
int<lower=1> J; // number of Individuals
int<lower=1> M; // number of Questions
int<lower=1> N; // number of observations
int<lower=1> K; // maximum number of categories
int<lower=1, upper=J> j[N]; // Individual for observation n
int<lower=1, upper=M> m[N]; // Question for observation n
int<lower=1, upper=K> y[N]; // Answer of observation n
int<lower=1, upper=K> k[M]; // Maximum categories of question m
int<lower=1, upper=K> q[N]; // Maximum categories of observation n
int<lower=1> D; //no. of dimensions
}
parameters {
matrix[M,K] alpha;
matrix[M,K] beta;
matrix[M,K] beta2;
matrix[J,D] theta;
}
model {
to_vector(alpha) ~ normal(0,1); 
for (i in 1:M){
alpha[i,1] ~ normal(0,0.000001);
for (g in (k[i]+1):K)
alpha[i,g] ~ normal(999,0.000001);} 

to_vector(beta) ~ normal(0,1); 
for (i in 1:M){
beta[i,1] ~ normal(0,0.000001);
for (g in (k[i]+1):K)
beta[i,g] ~ normal(999,0.000001);}

to_vector(beta2) ~ normal(0,1); 
for (i in 1:M){
beta2[i,1] ~ normal(0,0.000001);
for (g in (k[i]+1):K)
beta2[i,g] ~ normal(999,0.000001);}

to_vector(theta) ~ normal(0,0.1);  // priors

for (n in 1:N){
for (h in 1:q[n]){
y[n] ~ categorical(softmax(theta[j[n],1] * beta[m[n],h] + theta[j[n],2] * beta2[m[n],h] - alpha[m[n],h]));}
}


In JAGS, my model had a more complicated code to like the following.

for(i in 1:N){
  y[i] ~ dcat(prob[j[i],m[i],1:q[i]])
}

for (i in 1:N){
  for (h in 1:q[i]){
    p[j[i],m[i],h] <- exp(beta[m[i],h]*theta[j[i],1] + beta2[m[i],h]*theta[j[i],2] - alpha[m[i],k])
  }
  prob[j[i],m[i],1:q[i] ] <- p[j[i],m[i],1:q[i] ]/sum(p[j[i],m[i],1:q[i])
}

Do I have to run a similar code as I wrote in JAGS?
Is there a way that I use a more simpler code as I wrote above and do not get an error?

Thank you in advance!

By the way, maybe I'm wrong, but you are define twice alpha, beta and beta2.

messages.author: 61924cbc2e733aae
messages.subject: Re: Multinomial IRT model
parts: In the model block, you provide to the `categorical_logit(` or `categorical(softmax(` in the loop a scalar and you need to provide to each y[n] a vector. The inner loop need to be vectorized.
